- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

u**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

g**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

o**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

o**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

s**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

e**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

c**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

s**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

x**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

c**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

s**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

 **Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.

  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

a**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

g**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

/**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

***Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

a**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

P**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

r**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

o**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

s**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

,**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

d**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

d**Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

GPU acceleration happens in the viewer's browser. The server, for example wissi in Docker, needs no GPU. Run `wissi-viz bench … --headed` on a desktop to get numbers for your GPU.

  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.

***Benchmarks** (`wissi-viz bench`, see [benchmarks/](benchmarks/README.md)). Measured on a 2-vCPU cloud container with no GPU, where Chromium uses SwiftShader software WebGL:

- **Opening:** 8–17 ms for every file, including a 1.65 GB OME-TIFF.
- **Cold full-resolution tile:** 2.2 ms for SVS, 2.6 ms for OME-TIFF, 20 ms for CZI (a whole 2048² zstd subblock is decoded on first touch). A cached tile takes about 5 µs.
- **Panning:** the viewer's own JavaScript costs 0.2–5 ms per frame. The rest of each frame is rasterisation, which in this container is CPU-emulated.
  - At 800×500 a single pane pans at a locked 60 fps.
  - At 1600×1000 the frame rate is bound by software fill rate: a bare WebGL page manages only 20 fps here.
  - No run showed a blank area, at any pane count.
